query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Removing Co from the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy lowers its stacking fault energy, which in turn shifts the dominant deformation mechanism toward enhanced deformation twinning (with diminished cross‐slip) at lower temperatures and high strain rates. This switch in mechanism supports a superior strength–ductility balance when compared with the conventional Co-containing alloy, and its dynamic behavior will vary systematically with temperature and strain rate.
generation.material_initial_state: A single‐phase FCC Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy (derived by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi) with a similar grain size and processing history.
generation.intervention: Subject the Co-free alloy and a baseline Co-containing CoCrFeMnNi alloy to uniaxial mechanical testing across a range of temperatures (from room temperature up to 900 °C) and strain rates (from 10⁻³ to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹).
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile or compressive tests performed under controlled atmospheres at temperatures of 25 °C, intermediate temperatures, and up to 900 °C; strain rates varied from 10⁻³ s⁻¹ (slow) to 10⁻¹ s⁻¹ (fast).
generation.structural_mediator: A reduction in stacking fault energy leading to increased propensity for deformation twinning and reduced cross-slip, which governs dislocation interactions and work hardening.
generation.mechanism: The lower stacking fault energy in the Co-free alloy promotes earlier nucleation of twins at given stress levels, particularly at lower temperatures and higher strain rates. This nucleation retards dislocation recovery and enhances work hardening, thereby contributing to an improved strength–ductility trade-off. At elevated temperatures or lower strain rates, thermally activated slip and dynamic recovery override the twinning, shifting the balance toward increased ductility at a lower yield stress.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Co-containing baseline, the Co-free alloy will exhibit (a) higher yield strength and work hardening rates and clear microstructural evidence of deformation twinning under lower temperatures and higher strain rates; (b) a transition to lower yield strength with increased ductility at elevated temperatures or slower strain rates, aligning with dominant slip and recovery mechanisms.
generation.baseline: The conventional equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy processed under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: Applicable to single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys produced with similar grain sizes and heat treatments; valid over the temperature range of approximately 25 °C to 900 °C and strain rates between 10⁻³ and 10⁻¹ s⁻¹.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative differences in yield strength, work hardening, and ductility between the Co-free and Co-containing alloys are not fully predicted, as they depend on processing conditions and slight compositional variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one with the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy and one with the conventional CoCrFeMnNi alloy, ensuring identical processing and grain size. Perform uniaxial tensile (or compression) tests across temperatures from 25 °C to 900 °C and at strain rates of 10⁻³ s⁻¹ and 10⁻¹ s⁻¹. Use high-resolution electron microscopy (TEM/EBSD) to document deformation mechanisms (e.g., presence of twin boundaries) during and after deformation.
measurements: Microstructural characterization to detect deformation twins and dislocation structures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co-free alloy does not show an increased tendency for deformation twinning (i.e., no significant difference in twin density compared to the Co-containing alloy) and if its yield strength or work hardening behavior does not differ consistently from the baseline over the temperature and strain rate range, then the hypothesis that reduced stacking fault energy and enhanced twinning drive the superior strength–ductility balance would be falsified.

System: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA).
